done.why: I ran out of turns on the foot bridge, walking back to try the candy on the unicorn. I'd already reached most of what was open. Every other way forward ended in a rockfall that said it 'will have to wait'.

about: I'm treasure-hunting in caverns under a barrow. There's a formal garden, a spinning carousel room, a riddle door, a well you ride up in a bucket, and an Alice-in-Wonderland tea room with cakes that shrink and grow you. A meddling Wizard pops in to cast spells on me. Most of the puzzles are about working out what a thing is for: water raises the bucket, a robot takes orders, a flask works as a magnifying glass.

moments.note: The Wizard showed up, said 'Fantasize!' and vanished, and my sword glowed. It was ominous in a fun way.
The copy of ZORK I turned out to be a hallucination from the Wizard's spell, and the room 'has the grace to look embarrassed'. Lovely.
'answer "a well"' only got a hollow laugh. Plain 'answer well' worked on the next turn.
Poured water in the bucket and rode it up the well. 'Well done.' The pun landed.
The robot hurled the cage across the room and 'appears to be smiling'.
Reading the cakes through the flask worked, and they say Evaporate, Enlarge, Explode. That was a satisfying 'aha'.
Threw the red cake into the pool of tears and the candy appeared.
The orange cake crumbled to dust when I got in the bucket, and it wasn't clear why. I lost an item I hadn't figured out.
'fill teapot with water' said there was nothing to fill it with, even though the bucket held water. 'take water' worked.
The Carousel Room admitted the passages aren't identical after all, because I'd been thrown out so many times. It felt like the world noticed my effort.
Another way forward was blocked by a rockfall, 'will have to wait'. Third one.
Grabbing the unicorn's key made it vanish with a funny snub, but I had no idea what to do instead.

wished: I wished I knew where treasures are meant to go. There was no trophy case or obvious place to bring them.
I wished there was a way to win over the unicorn. I ran out of turns before I could try the candy.
I wished I could get through the blocked passages: the carousel's rockfalls and the ledge above the deep ford.
I wished the carousel didn't make getting around so slow. A lot of my turns went on retracing steps through random exits.
I wished 'answer "a well"' had been accepted.

lines.line: It was never there: the Wizard's word put it in the room, and the room, having no say in the matter, let it, and has the grace to look embarrassed about it now.
lines.why: It was funny, and it told me what the Wizard's spell actually did.

lines.line: the rope above it is taut as though it would like to again.
lines.why: A clue that read like prose. It pointed me to water.

lines.line: You are at the top of the well. Well done.
The cage shakes and is hurled across the room. It's hard to say, but the robot appears to be smiling.
lines.why: The robot came across as a character.

lines.line: You have been thrown out of here enough times now to have noticed that the passages are not quite identical after all: three of them end in rock, and one, on the southeast side, climbs.
lines.why: The world rewarded me for persisting and gave me a map hint.

lines.line: The unicorn, unsurprised by this evidence that you are indeed the uncouth sort of vagabond it suspected you were, melts into the hedges and is gone.
lines.why: A failure that made me laugh.

fun.why: Several real aha moments: the bucket, the robot and cage, the cakes read through the flask. The carousel wandering dragged.

engagement.why: I always had a next goal: the bucket, then the robot, then the cakes, then the unicorn. The pull slackened only near the end, when I hit rockfalls.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were fair, and the clues showed up in the descriptions. A couple of parser phrasings tripped me, and the unicorn left me stumped.

interestingness.why: The hallucination, the Wonderland cakes and the self-aware carousel all made it feel more than a straight retread.

prose.why: The added lines are witty and precise, and some of them double as clues. The embarrassed room and the snobbish unicorn stood out.
